column1: There are some discoveries in advanced mathematics that do not depend on specialized knowledge, not even on algebra, geometry, or trigonometry.

column1: Instead they may involve, at most, a little arithmetic, such as ‘the sum of two odd numbers is even’, and common sense.
column2: 这些发现最多只需要一点算术，例如“两个奇数之和为偶数”，再加上常识就够了。

column1: Each of the eight chapters in this book illustrates this phenomenon.

column1: Anyone can understand every step in the reasoning.

column1: Thus all readers will have the chance to participate in a mathematical experience, to appreciate the beauty of mathematics, and to become familiar with its logical, yet intuitive, style of thinking.
column2: 这样，所有读者都有机会亲自体验数学、欣赏数学之美，熟悉那种既合乎逻辑又依靠直觉的思考方式。

column1: One of my purposes in writing this book is to give readers who haven’t had the opportunity to see and enjoy real mathematics the chance to appreciate the mathematical way of thinking.
column2: 我写这本书的一个目的，是让那些一直无缘领略真正数学之趣的读者，也有机会体会数学的思考方式。

column1: I want to reveal not only some of the fascinating discoveries, but, more importantly, the reasoning behind them.
column2: 我想展示的不只是一些迷人的发现，更重要的是这些发现背后的推理。
column6: reasoning behind them|这些发现背后的推理

column1: In that respect, this book differs from most books on mathematics written for the general public.
column2: 在这一点上，这本书与大多数写给普通大众的数学书有所不同。

column1: Some present the lives of colorful mathematicians.
column2: 有的书讲述富有个性的数学家们的人生。

column1: Others describe important applications of mathematics.
column2: 有的书描述数学的重要应用。

column1: Yet others go into mathematical procedures, but assume that the reader is adept in using algebra.
column2: 还有的书深入讲解数学运算过程，却默认读者能熟练运用代数。

column1: I hope this book will help bridge that notorious gap that separates the two cultures: the humanities and the sciences, or should I say the right brain (intuitive) and the left brain (analytical, numerical).
column2: 我希望这本书能帮助弥合那道尽人皆知的隔阂，它分开了人文学科与自然科学这两种文化；或者，我是否该说，它分开了凭直觉的右脑与擅长分析和数字的左脑？

column1: As the chapters will illustrate, mathematics is not restricted to the analytical and numerical; intuition plays a significant role.

column1: The alleged gap can be narrowed or completely overcome by anyone, in part because each of us is far from using the full capacity of either side of the brain.

column1: To illustrate our human potential, I cite a structural engineer who is an artist, an electrical engineer who is an opera singer, an opera singer who published mathematical research, and a mathematician who publishes short stories.

column1: Other scientists have written books to explain their fields to non-scientists, but have necessarily had to omit the mathematics, although it provides the foundation of their theories.
column2: 其他科学家也曾著书向非科学专业的读者介绍自己的领域，但尽管数学是其理论的基础，他们在写作中却不得不把数学部分省去。

column1: The reader must remain a tantalized spectator rather than an involved participant, since the appropriate language for describing the details in much of science is mathematics, whether the subject is expanding universe, subatomic particles, or chromosomes.
column2: 于是，读者只能做一个兴趣被吊起却无法亲自参与的旁观者。这是因为，无论讨论的是膨胀的宇宙、亚原子粒子还是染色体，数学都是描述众多科学领域细节的合适语言。

column1: Though the broad outline of a scientific theory can be sketched intuitively, when a part of the physical universe is finally understood, its description often looks like a page in a mathematics text.
column2: 科学理论的大致轮廓虽可凭直觉勾勒出来，但物质宇宙的某一部分一旦最终为人理解，描述它的文字往往看上去就像数学课本里的一页。

column1: Still, the non-mathematical reader can go far in understanding mathematical reasoning.

column1: As I wrote, I kept in mind two types of readers: those who enjoyed mathematics until they were turned off by an unpleasant episode, usually around fifth grade, and mathematics aficionados, who will find much that is new throughout the book.
column2: 写作时，我心里想着两类读者：一类人原来喜欢数学，后来却因一次不愉快的经历而失去兴趣，这种经历通常发生在小学五年级前后；另一类是数学爱好者，他们会在书中各处遇到不少新鲜内容。

column1: This book also serves readers who simply want to sharpen their analytical skills.

column1: Each chapter offers practice in following a sustained and closely argued line of thought.
